title: An arrow can wear a different head, and its pill can be a badge or a pill
goal: Every arrow ends in the same solid triangle, and every caption sits in the same fully rounded pill. Give the arrow a choice of endings, a solid triangle, a fine open one, a solid dot, a hollow dot and a plain line, and let the caption corner be adjusted from square through rounded to fully round, so a label can read as a badge or as a pill.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-05. Today AnnotationStyles carries only arrowheadScale (Sources/PhotonzCore/AnnotationStyles.swift, coding key arrowheadScale, defaultArrowheadScale) and there is no notion of a head SHAPE; the rasterizer draws one triangle. Add a head style to AnnotationContent with the triangle as the decoded default so old documents are untouched, and a corner radius for the caption pill likewise defaulting to fully round. Both belong in the tool options for the arrow, drawn as glyphs; see how the measure tool shows its modes for the pattern. Depends on the arrow polish task landing first so the pill is being drawn from one place before its shape becomes adjustable.
acceptance: The arrow settings offer a set of endings shown as pictures rather than words, and picking one changes the arrow at once
Each ending scales with the stroke width the way the current triangle does, and stays centred on the point it marks
The caption corner is adjustable from square to fully round, with the current fully round look as the default
Both settings are remembered as the default for the next arrow you draw, the way colour and thickness already are
An arrow saved before this opens with the triangle and the round pill it had, unchanged
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation
Audit written under queue/audits/ showing every ending at two stroke widths and a caption at three corner settings, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Triage 2026-09-06: its dep named a-captioned-arrow-sits-right-tight-selection-a but the task that landed is a-captioned-arrow-sits-right-tight-selection-a-p, so this was the one open task the loop could never claim. Dep repointed. Epic moved off epic-uehjr1 (staged later) onto measure-redline, which is staged now, because the user asked for this on 2026-09-05.

Adversarial review before building. (1) Five endings, and only the HEAD end wears one: the tail is where the caption pill hangs from, so a second control for it would fight the label. Shortest version that delivers the value. (2) 'A plain line' is no ornament at all, which makes an arrow that is just a leader line with a label on it: the redline case where you point at something and let the caption do the talking. It does overlap the Line tool, but a Line cannot carry a caption, so it earns its place. (3) The round endings are the trap: a triangle's TIP sits on the point it marks, a dot's CENTRE does, so a dot reaches past the endpoint and the layer frame has to grow or the ink clips. Frame padding and drawn bounds both get head-aware reach. (4) A hollow dot with the shaft running into it looks like a lollipop with a stick through it, so the shaft stops on the ring's near edge; the open head keeps the shaft to the tip, because that is what makes it read as one V. (5) Storing the caption corner in POINTS would be wrong: the same 8pt corner is a badge at 20px text and nearly square at 60px, so a label resize would silently change its shape. It is stored as roundness, 0 square to 1 fully round, which also makes 'unchanged for old arrows' free. (6) Cut from the mock idea: no separate tail ending, no per-end control, no numeric corner field. Two controls, five pictures and one slider.

Built and reviewed on the real app. Five endings (solid head, open head, solid dot, hollow dot, plain line) live on AnnotationContent.arrowheadStyle, decoding to the solid head so older documents are untouched; the caption corner is AnnotationContent.captionRoundness, 0 square to 1 fully round, decoding to 1. Geometry owns the shapes: arrowheadCircle, arrowheadReach, arrowheadBounds, and arrowShaftEnd now takes a style, so the shaft stops inside a solid head, at the tip of an open one and on the near edge of a hollow dot. Frame padding and drawn bounds grew head-aware, which a dot needs because it hangs past the point it marks. Both settings ride in ShapeDefaults so the next arrow inherits them. Rows: Ending (a row of pictures, with the picked one named in words beside its caption) and Label corners (Square through Pill), in the dock and, for the ending, in the arrow tool's own settings; Head Size hides itself for a plain ending. SECOND REVIEW, on the built thing: (a) the dot came out NARROWER than a heavy line, so at 20pt it read as a bulge rather than a mark. Round endings got their own floor, never narrower than twice the shaft, and there is a test for it. (b) The picker floated in the middle of a column of full-width sliders; it now claims the row and sits at its leading edge. (c) A row of pictures gets one tooltip for the whole row, so no single picture can explain itself. The word beside the caption carries the meaning instead, and the per-picture tooltip is filed as each-picture-in-a-row-of-pictures-says-its-own-n. Harness: press now takes an "across" fraction, because a slider could only ever be pressed halfway and the square corner was therefore unprovable by a walk. Walk: Scripts/playtest/arrow-endings-walk.json. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-06-arrow-endings.json with two real screen captures and a rendered contact sheet.
